history: Found as a CRASH INSIDE A REFUSAL. The typer correctly decided the value did not fit in int64 and then wrote its diagnosis -- f'integer literal {e.value} does not fit in int64' -- and interpolating a 20,000-bit integer into an f-string IS a decimal conversion, which is the thing CPython caps at 4300 digits. The ValueError was raised from inside the raise. The verdict was right and the sentence explaining it is what fell over, on the branch that only ever runs on input somebody else wrote.
note: Hex is the door the decimal limit does not cover: CPython caps decimal conversion and not base 16, so a 20,000-bit literal used to walk in unchallenged and only be rejected later. Now the digit count is checked on the way in, whatever the base.
